name: Wyclef Jean
description:
'''Nelust Wyclef Jean''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|w|aɪ|k|l|ɛ|f|_|ˈ|ʒ|ɒ|n}} {{Respell|WY|klef|_|ZHON}}; born October 17, 1969) is a Haitian rapper, singer, songwriter and music producer. He gained fame as a member of [[Fugees]]. Their second album [[The Score (Fugees album)|''The Score'']] (1996) became one of the [[best-selling albums of all time]]. He launched a solo career with ''[[Wyclef Jean Presents The Carnival]]'' (1997), featuring the single "[[We Trying to Stay Alive]]", the [[Grammy Awards|Grammy]]-nominated "[[Guantanamera#Wyclef Jean version|Guantanamera]]" featuring [[Celia Cruz]] and [[Lauryn Hill]], and the top ten hit "[[Gone till November]]".  

His second album, ''[[The Ecleftic: 2 Sides II a Book]]'' (2000), included the R&B hit "[[911 (Wyclef Jean song)|911]]" featuring [[Mary J. Blige]]. His third album, [[Masquerade (Wyclef Jean album)|''Masquerade'']] (2002), peaked within the top ten of the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]], and spawned the top 40 single "[[Two Wrongs]]" with [[Claudette Ortiz]]. He made a guest appearance on the 2006 single "[[Hips Don't Lie]]" by [[Shakira]], which became a global success, reaching number one in 18 countries. His song "[[Sweetest Girl (Dollar Bill)]]" with [[Akon]], [[Lil Wayne]] and [[Niia]], served as the lead single for his sixth studio album ''[[Carnival Vol. II: Memoirs of an Immigrant]]'' (2007). He released "[[Dar um Jeito (We Will Find a Way)]]", the official [[2014 FIFA World Cup]] anthem alongside [[Carlos Santana]], [[Avicii]], and [[Alexandre Pires]]. 

Jean has [[Wyclef Jean discography#Production discography|produced and co-written several songs for other artists]], including [[Destiny's Child]]'s first hit "[[No, No, No (Destiny's Child song)|No, No, No]]" remix, "[[My Love Is Your Love (song)|My Love Is Your Love]]" by [[Whitney Houston]], "[[Maria Maria]]" by [[Santana (band)|Santana]], "[[Ghetto Supastar (That Is What You Are)]]" by [[Pras]] featuring [[Ol' Dirty Bastard]] and [[Mya (singer)|Mya]], and "[[What Would You Do? (City High song)|What Would You Do?]]" by [[City High]]. Furthermore, he composed the score for the 2003 film ''[[The Agronomist]]''. His accolades include three [[Grammy Award]]s, the [[BET Humanitarian Award]] and the [[NAACP Image Awards|NAACP Vanguard Award]]. He received a [[Golden Globe Awards|Golden Globe]] nomination for [[Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song|Best Original Song]] for co-writing the song "Million Voices" for ''[[Hotel Rwanda]]'' (2004). 

Jean has been also active in [[Politics of Haiti|Haitian politics]] and philanthropy. In 1999, he released the [[Charity record|charity single]] "[[New Day (Wyclef Jean song)|New Day]]" alongside [[Bono]]. He was appointed [[Ambassador-at-large|Ambassador-at-Large]] of Haiti in 2007 and later ran for the [[Haitian general election, 2010|2010 Haitian presidency]], but was deemed ineligible due to residency requirements. His charity, [[Yéle Haiti]], raised funds for Haitian relief efforts, including the [[2010 Haitian earthquake]], before disbanding amid financial scrutiny. Haitian President [[Michel Martelly]] awarded him the [[National Order of Honour and Merit]].
